note: The decision-readiness register: the questions that must be answered before a reasonable decision can be made, what information we already have, what is missing, and how to discover it. Each question names the decision it blocks and where the answer should be recorded. Review alongside suggestions/index.html — choosing a path there may depend on answers here.

questions.question: Are the five submitted short links Associates-generated Special Links carrying tracking ID shopnow047c-20?
we_know: All five URLs live under the .amazon gTLD operated by Amazon Registry Services, Inc. [S09].
Observation 2026-11-20: four of five resolved to amazon.com product pages; none of the observed landing URLs contained a tag=shopnow047c-20 parameter [FLG-003].
The Operating Agreement pays commission only on purchases that follow 'a Special Link' using its special tagged link formats [S01, S03].
questions.missing: Whether each submitted link was generated inside Associates Central (SiteStripe / Link Builder) and whether clicks through it attribute to shopnow047c-20.
discovery: Associates Central → Reports → 'Links' or 'Clicks' history: click one link from the site and check whether the click is attributed.
Rebuild one link per product with SiteStripe 'Get link' and compare destination + tracking ID.
Do not merge intent with observation: record observed targets only in the observation field of data/products.json.
questions.blocks: Whether public CTAs can be marked 'verified'; any conversion measurement we can trust.

questions.question: Is tracking ID shopnow047c-20 enrolled and active, and for which marketplace?
we_know: The ID was supplied in the brief; the '-20' suffix is the conventional US marketplace indicator, but this is convention, not verification.
No official source was reachable that could confirm the ID's existence or status (Associates Central is account-gated) [FLG-001].
questions.missing: Enrollment status, account standing, and the exact marketplace(s) the ID applies to.
questions.discovery: Associates Central → Settings → Account info: confirm the tracked ID, marketplace, and payment status; screenshot for the review record.
questions.blocks: Everything downstream: attribution, reporting, Creators API prerequisites [S13].

questions.question: Which exact products do the five submitted links intend? Do the observed landing ASINs match the intended ones?
we_know: Submitted path identifiers are 9 characters; Amazon's official ASIN definition is 10 characters [S05].

Observed landing ASINs (10 characters) differ from the submitted path identifiers in every case where a landing page was observed: B04G1MEwY→B0CDY277D3, B02NbDxp3→B09B7SB46R, B00hJ57DV→B08DKYBTPH, B0f3GKalj→B0DZFD6R9Z; B0c8moW59 unresolved [FLG-003, FLG-004].
Intent and observation are kept in separate fields and never merged (products.json rules).
questions.missing: Confirmation that each observed landing listing is the product the submitter intended.
discovery: Ask the link submitter for the original product page URLs or a screenshot of each SiteStripe generation.
Once Creators API access is active, one GetItems call per ASIN confirms identity, title, and price [S13].
questions.blocks: Product profiles' verified fields; comparison table; any 'best for' claims about specific products.

questions.question: What is the actual niche and category scope the site should publish against?
we_know: Four of the five observed landings are air fryers (dual-basket, oven-style French-door, family-size basket) and one is a wireless meat thermometer — consistent with the brief's air-fryer editorial hypotheses [FLG-003 observations].
The four guide working titles supplied in the brief are all air-fryer/kitchen-appliance questions.
questions.missing: Confirmation that the observed landings equal the intended products (see Q-03) — the niche plan is hypothesis, not fact, until then.
questions.discovery: Confirm Q-03 first. Then validate the four published guides' topics against the confirmed product set before adding clusters.
questions.blocks: Editorial calendar priorities; cluster expansion (e.g., 'Prep & precision' stays second fiddle if the thermometer is not intended).

questions.question: Where should the self-hosted analytics endpoint live, and who owns it?
we_know: GitHub Pages is static hosting; the endpoint needs a server component elsewhere [S10].
The five defined events and a local-queue fallback already ship (analytics.js).
questions.missing: A hosting + ownership decision (options A/B/C on the suggestion board, SG-08).
questions.discovery: Choose an option on suggestions/index.html; wire window.SHOPNOW_CONFIG.analyticsEndpoint; keep the queue as fallback.
questions.blocks: Real click/conversion measurement; ledger population; measured topic selection.

questions.question: When will product-data automation be possible (Creators API), and what do we need first?
we_know: PA-API 5.0 is deprecated; the supported path is the Creators API [S12, S13].
Prerequisites per official docs: Associates enrollment for the target marketplace and at least 10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days [S13].
questions.missing: Current sales history (account-gated), which gates the API threshold.
questions.discovery: Associates Central → Reports: check the trailing-30-day qualifying-sales figure; when ≥10, register for the Creators API through Associates Central.
questions.blocks: Automated price/spec refresh; verified comparison table; drop of manual verification steps.

questions.question: What imagery may the site use?
we_know: All site imagery is AI-generated and labeled as illustrative; no Amazon product imagery, logos, or marks are used (Participation Requirements restrict use of Amazon marks and Content to the licensed scope) [S01, S02].
questions.missing: A decision on future imagery: keep AI-generated illustrative art, add original photography, or license stock.
questions.discovery: Decide on the suggestion board (SG-10); update the imagery note in about/index.html in the same change.
questions.blocks: Product-card visuals once listings are verified (product photos are NOT usable except via licensed Content formats).

questions.question: Where should reader capture (email) deliveries go, and with which provider?
we_know: The capture form currently queues nothing external: it records a reader_capture event and shows a confirmation. No address leaves the browser.

Associates rules prohibit affiliate links in email unless a separate written agreement exists [S02, clause 6] — the newsletter design keeps links on the site, not in email bodies, until that agreement exists.
questions.missing: A provider/destination decision (static-site compatible options: Buttondown, Listmonk, Formspree-class services).
questions.discovery: Pick one on the suggestion board (SG-11); wire the form action; keep the privacy note accurate.

questions.question: What publishing cadence should the site commit to?
we_know: Four question-shaped guides published 2026-11-20; a seasonal calendar sketch exists on guides/index.html.
The brief's own principle: the next topic should be chosen from measured queries, not instinct.
questions.missing: A cadence the maintainer can sustain (weekly/biweekly), and Search Console data to choose topics from (needs Q-10 first).
questions.discovery: Commit to a cadence on the suggestion board (SG-12); re-evaluate after 30 days of Search Console query data.
questions.blocks: Editorial calendar; feed expectations for returning readers.

questions.question: Who owns Search Console verification for the Pages property?
we_know: Verification methods and steps are documented by Google [S11]; the site head carries a ready placeholder for the HTML-tag method.
Verification requires a Google account the site owner controls — it cannot be completed by this session.
questions.missing: A Google account holder performing HTML-tag verification for https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil3/ (and later the sitemap submission).
questions.discovery: Follow search-console/index.html step by step (10 minutes).
